motion.name: LineReveal
motion.value: y 105% to 0 behind an overflow mask, 600ms, delay 100ms plus 90ms per line
motion.purpose: h1 lines only. Reduced motion renders in place.

motion.name: Spine
motion.value: scaleY bound to scroll progress, offset start 0.75 to end 0.55

motion.name: no-js
motion.purpose: Every animated element carries data-reveal so content shows without JavaScript.

narrative.overview:
Paper being set down on a desk. Forest, pine and moss greens on warm chalk and paper grounds, with hairline rules doing the work that boxes and shadows do elsewhere. The type is editorial. A Newsreader display at weight 500 carries every headline, Geist sets the reading text, and Geist Mono marks things: timeline stages, status, prices, navigation, small print. The page reads like a well-made printed brief, not a product dashboard.

Density is low and vertical. Sections are long, single-column or split 3:9 on a 12-column grid, and separated by changes of ground (chalk, haze, forest) rather than by borders or cards. Color is almost entirely green and neutral. Each screen gets one accent beat: claret on light grounds, ochre on forest. Depth is nearly flat: real screenshots sit in a 2px frame with a hairline and a soft shadow, and nothing else floats.

Motion is quiet and one-directional. Things rise a few pixels into place once and stay put. The homepage's signature is the timeline spine: a pine line draws down a hairline as the journey scrolls through view.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white grounds only (chalk page, paper cards). Never pure white.
Green carries headings, buttons, links and rules. One accent beat per screen.
Newsreader 500 display with at most one italic word per composition.
Geist Mono for markers, status, prices and nav. Lists use a mono plus sign.
2px corners, 3px chips, pills only on buttons. Hairline rules over boxes.
No gradients, no glows. Shadows at 12% opacity or less.
Every service carries a "Live" or "Ask us" tag, nothing else.

rules.name: The One Beat Rule
rules.body: Each screen gets a single accent beat: claret on light grounds, ochre on forest. If claret already appears in the frame (the hero's italic "mind"), nothing else on that screen is claret at rest. Hover, focus and error states are the only exceptions.

rules.name: The Never White Rule
rules.body: Grounds are chalk, paper, stone, haze or forest. Pure #FFFFFF never ships on the brand layer.

rules.name: The Ink Mute Rule
rules.body: Ink mute is for icons and rules. Any text that needs to be read uses ink-soft or darker.

rules.name: The One Italic Rule
rules.body: At most one italic word per composition, and it carries the accent. Italics are never used for emphasis in body copy.

rules.name: The Mono Marks Rule
rules.body: Mono text marks a thing (a stage, a status, a price, a link destination). It never introduces a heading from above. A small uppercase label sitting directly over an h1 or h2 is an eyebrow, and eyebrows are banned. Markers in the spine's own column, meta lines after content, captions and footer group titles are the mono's native uses and stay.

rules.name: The Full Stop Rule
rules.body: Headlines are short declaratives that end in a full stop, set with balanced wrapping.

rules.name: The Ground Change Rule
rules.body: Sections are divided by switching ground (chalk to haze to forest), not by boxing content in cards. A forest section directly above the forest footer gets a hairline (chalk at 10%) between them.

rules.name: The Twelve Percent Rule
rules.body: No shadow exceeds 12% opacity, and none is colored. No gradients, no glows, no hard offset shadows.

rules.name: The Pill Is A Button Rule
rules.body: If it is pill-shaped, it is pressable and it is a button. Tags, chips, cards and images never round past 3px.

dos: **Do** use the v7 color names (forest, pine, chalk, ink-soft and the rest) or the semantic CSS aliases in all new brand-layer code.
**Do** keep one accent beat per screen: claret on light grounds, ochre on forest.
**Do** put forest sections in `.on-inverse` so headings, links, focus and accent re-point together.

**Do** keep a 44px minimum touch target on every link and control. Links on their own line use `.d-link` with `inline-block`; nav, footer and breadcrumb links use a 44px minimum height or negative-margin padding.
**Do** use PlusList (mono "+", hairline rows) for every list of points.
**Do** tag every service "Live" or "Ask us" with StatusTag, and leave out anything that is neither.
**Do** wrap scroll-in content in Reveal, h1 lines in LineReveal, and add `data-reveal` to any new animated element so the no-JS rule covers it.
**Do** frame real screenshots in ImageFrame: 2px corner, rule-soft hairline, Card shadow.
donts: **Don't** use the legacy Tailwind aliases (primary, accent, dark, surface, warm, border, border-strong, text-primary, text-secondary, text-muted, status, shadow-soft, shadow-medium) in new code. They exist only so /onboard, /admin, /upload and /demo stay on-palette untouched.
**Don't** put a mono eyebrow label above a heading. InnerHero's `eyebrow` prop is accepted and never rendered.
**Don't** use gradients, glows, colored shadows, or any shadow above 12% opacity.
**Don't** use tick or check icons in lists; use the mono plus sign.
**Don't** set more than one italic word in a composition, or use claret and ochre on the same screen.
**Don't** add CSS keyframe animation to elements already driven by framer-motion.
